subject: Private offer — term concession request & buyer approval path
messages:
From: Devon Reed <devon.reed@finovate.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-09T16:14:00Z
Subject: Inquiry: private offer term flexibility and approval routing

Hi Markus,

We’re evaluating Redwood for batch inference in a pilot across three business units. Procurement asked me to check whether you can accommodate a 9-month private offer (instead of the standard 12) with a modest price concession. Key constraints:

- Our CFO needs to review anything above $120k ARR-equivalent (procurement will route).
- We have a multi-account setup and would prefer a delegated buyer workflow if possible.
- We’ll need SOC2 evidence and an estimated activation timeline to include in the PO.

Can Redwood create a private offer that: 1) supports a 9-month commit with pro-rated billing; 2) includes a short approval path we can present to our CFO; and 3) indicates expected activation lead time?

I attached Finovate’s procurement guidelines for reference. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Devon Reed
Head of Cloud Procurement
Finovate Systems

Attachment: procurement_guidelines.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Devon Reed <devon.reed@finovate.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-09T18:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Inquiry: private offer term flexibility and approval routing

Hi Devon — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing procurement’s doc. Short answer: yes, we can structure a private offer for a 9-month commit, but there are trade-offs and an approval gating we’ll need to follow. High-level options:

Option A — 9-month pilot (recommended):
- Price: ~8–12% uplift vs. 12-month list to account for shorter term (we can tighten after seeing usage).
- Activation: ~5 business days after signed private offer + AWS activation window.
- Approval: standard delegated buyer flow works if procurement confirms delegated-account IDs. CFO review only required if ARR-equivalent > $120k.

Option B — 9-month with conditional conversion to 12-month:
- Lower uplift if buyer commits to automatic conversion at month 9 (requires a DocuSign amendment).

I’m attaching a preliminary pricing worksheet so you can see ballpark figures. If you confirm procurement contact and delegated accounts, I’ll loop in our marketplace ops team to scope activation and approve the nonstandard term.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm (a) billed amount threshold tolerance, (b) delegated buyer account IDs, and (c) whether a conversion clause is acceptable.
2) I’ll create a DocuSign draft and loop Marketplace Ops (Vanessa) for activation SLAs and legal signoff.

Cc’ing Grace — she’ll help with usage-profile guidance so we can optimize the price/term trade-off.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: prelim_pricing.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Devon Reed <devon.reed@finovate.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@finovate.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Inquiry: private offer term flexibility and approval routing

Thanks Markus — that helps. A few clarifications from procurement:

- The CFO threshold is firm at $120k. If the 9-month total spend is under that, they’ll accept delegated buyer approvals.
- Delegated accounts: acct-135, acct-136, acct-142 (we’ll send formal IDs in a follow-up).
- Conversion clause is acceptable, but procurement needs the wording up front (they want a clear amendment flow).

Can you include suggested PO wording for the conversion and a one-page activation timeline we can attach to the private offer? Procurement copied on this thread is Rebecca (procure@finovate.com).

Devon

Attachment: procurement_guidelines.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Reed <devon.reed@finovate.com>, Procurement Team <procure@finovate.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T16:05:00Z
Subject: FW: Private offer — term concession request & buyer approval path

Vanessa / Grace — looping you both in to advise on operational feasibility and to draft the PO wording. Context: Finovate (external) is requesting a 9-month private offer with either a price uplift or a conditional conversion to a 12-month commit at month 9. Key constraints: CFO signoff only if total > $120k; delegated account routing (acct-135/136/142) is acceptable; procurement needs a one-page activation timeline and SOC2 evidence.

Recommended path from Sales:
- Create a private offer with a 9-month pilot price (8% uplift) and optional auto-convert clause to 12 months at a reduced rate if the buyer signs the amendment before month 9.
- Use delegated buyer flow for activation; require CFO signature only if projected spend > $120k (we’ll include a clear spend threshold clause).
- Prepare DocuSign draft + AWS PO instructions and a one-page timeline for procurement.

If Ops confirms the activation window and any special AWS console steps, we’ll produce the DocuSign bundle and send to Devon + Rebecca. Proposed deal id RDW-2026-5098.

Markus

(Internal note: attach prelim_pricing.xlsx to the DocuSign packet; include SOC2 link in the evidence bundle.)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Reed <devon.reed@finovate.com>, Procurement Team <procure@finovate.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: FW: Private offer — term concession request & buyer approval path

Thanks for the context. Operational notes below:

- Activation lead time: standard AWS private offer activation is 3–7 business days after DocuSign + AWS acceptance (we’ll plan for 7).
- Approval tiers: delegated buyer activation is supported for the acct-* IDs Devon listed; procurement must provide exact delegated buyer IAM/Account IDs for the AWS flow.
- Billing: pro-rated billing across the 9-month period is fine; we’ll include proration language in the PO.
- SOC2 / evidence: attach SOC2 report + audit summary in the DocuSign packet; use our evidence link (internal) — I’ve added it to the HubSpot deal.

Attachments I’ll include in the outbound packet:
- aws_po_instructions.md (how Finovate accepts and activates the PO)
- activation_timeline.png (one-page visual timeline)

I’ll draft the PO wording for the auto-convert clause (simple: "If Buyer elects conversion prior to month 9, Seller will apply the agreed annual rate from month 1 onward upon execution of the amendment") and circulate for legal review.

Region: us (per Devon).

Vanessa Ortiz
Marketplace Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: aws_po_instructions.md (text/markdown), activation_timeline.png (image/png)
